purpose: Specify required behavior for dirty-file content and provider unavailability so Stage 2-6 arbitration and freshness policies degrade explicitly and never fabricate exact authority.

dirty_file_behavior.scenario: SCIP artifact digest does not match current workspace file content
dirty_file_behavior.given: src/example/OrderService.java edited after the SCIP artifact was produced

expected.fallback: structural (tree-sitter) or heuristic (regex) with explicit degradation
expected.index_result: must still index; must not fail the file or the whole index

dirty_file_behavior.scenario: LSP live overlay document version matches dirty buffer
dirty_file_behavior.given: open document version / content digest matches the indexed source

expected.reproducibility: batch snapshot with overlay disabled remains reproducible

expected.must_not: silently claim tree-sitter ran or elevate regex output to structural/exact

provider_unavailability.current_ground_truth: java/typescript parse-file already emit these reason codes and fall back to regex today

provider_unavailability.scenario: SCIP artifact absent for a file

expected.index_result: no index failure; degradation reported additively

provider_unavailability.scenario: LSP server crash or timeout mid-request

expected.must_not: fail unrelated files or the whole index
expected.authority_after: fall back to SCIP/tree-sitter/regex per plan

authority_invariants: Regex-produced semantic facts are always heuristic or fallback; never exact.
Lower authority may fill missing facts but must never overwrite a higher-authority value.
Equal-authority contradictions are surfaced as explicit ambiguity, not resolved by registration/completion order.
Unknown or stale source identity cannot produce exact facts.
